abstract: A group of professionals working in dailies around the world have identified a need for consistency across the industry, forming a working group to create open databases and references. Dailies are a part of the production process that may be done in one or more regions, often utilizing freelance talent and requiring a significant amount of time and resources for specialized training. Therefore, streamlining this part of a workflow has major cost-saving potential. Focusing initially on Dailies Quality Control (QC), the working group has identified and built a database of taxonomy and definitions as well as determined best practices and recommendations that are consistent and applicable to all projects regardless of studio, type, location, or scale.

authors.bio: Isaac Spedding is a New Zealand dailies colorist who works with The Rebel Fleet and is passionate about production workflow, technology, and the development of the industry with 14 years of production experience around the globe. He also consults for production companies to train skilled crew and develop future focused workflows. He supports gender equality, and tries to incorporate Tikanga in the aspects of his work. Notable productions include The Lord of The Rings Series for Amazon Prime, Netflix’s KATE, Disney’s Mulan, Wellington Paranormal, The World Economic Forum, and TEDx Scott Base.
authors.name: Isaac Spedding

authors.bio: David Hall is part of the production workflow team at Netflix, focusing on guidance and information about the real-world implementation of technology on productions, while also acting as an advocate for innovation. Prior to joining Netflix, he spent a number of years at a post-production facility providing workflow oversight for dailies teams both in-facility and remote. In that capacity, he had the privilege to dig into creative workflow for projects such as Tenet, Dune, The Mandalorian, Westworld, and El Camino: A Breaking Bad Movie. He holds degrees in sociology and communications from Tulane University, New Orleans, LA.
authors.name: David Hall

authors.bio: Katie Hinsen is an award-winning production technology executive with an extensive background as a finishing artist, engineer, editor, visual effects artist, and colorist. She is a passionate mentor and advocate for emerging talent, and the co-founder of Blue Collar Post Collective. As director of technology for Marvel Studios, she is deeply engaged in the technical innovations that are transforming the entertainment industry and dedicated to supporting the teams of talent who dare to challenge what is possible.
authors.name: Katie Hinsen

authors.bio: James Elliston is a freelance dailies colorist and digital imaging technician in Auckland, New Zealand. His credits include The Wilds, Sweet Tooth, and No Exit
authors.name: James Elliston
